source_text: VI. Passus est autem beatissimus Cyprianus martyr die octava decima kalendarum Octobrium sub Valeriano et Gallieno imperatoribus, regnante vero domino nostro Iesu Christo; cui est honor et gloria in saecula saeculorum, amen.
thought_title: Date of death and closing praise
orientation: The narrator closes the account after Cyprian has been executed and buried by giving the date of his death.
pass_a_gloss: But the most blessed Cyprian the martyr suffered on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October under Valerian and Gallienus as emperors, with our lord Jesus Christ in contrast reigning; to whom is honor and glory into ages of ages, amen.

lemmas.gloss: martyr, one who dies for witness
Kalends, first day of the month

choices.why: keeps literal sense of patior for the death without adding a method of killing not stated in this clause
keeps superlative force of beatissimus and keeps martyr as a title in apposition

choices.english: on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October
choices.why: renders Roman backward date reckoning literally without converting to a modern calendar date

choices.term: regnante vero domino nostro Iesu Christo
choices.english: with our lord Jesus Christ in contrast reigning
choices.why: keeps ablative absolute and contrast force of vero against the emperors named just before
rejected: though our lord Jesus Christ reigns
in the reign of our lord Jesus Christ

choices.why: keeps literal plural repetition of saeculum without polishing to an English idiom

pass_b_english: Most blessed Cyprian the martyr suffered on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October under the emperors Valerian and Gallienus, but our Lord Jesus Christ reigns, to whom belong honor and glory for ages of ages, amen.
